transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (AetherScale), Liam O'Connor (AetherScale), Sara Venkatesh (AetherScale)

Summary:
Brief partner intro focused on GPU onramp patterns, reseller vs integration models, and pilot/benchmark requirements. Action items and next steps agreed (see metadata).

Topics:
- Partnership models (reseller, onramp, integration joint go-to-market)
- Technical integration: GPU compatibility, network/NICs, VPC/private deployments, on-prem package
- Security/compliance and telemetry expectations
- Pilot scope and success criteria, benchmarks and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you taking time. Quick round of intros, we'll do a 45-ish minute intro and then dig into technical bits. Diego, want to intro yourself briefly?
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Yeah, hi all. Diego, SE at Redwood, focus on performance and infra integrations — benchmarks, aporting kv-cache and batching stuff, that sort of thing.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here, head of partnerships at AetherScale. We're the company that sells GPU bricks and an onramp service for enterprise customers.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Liam, I run GPU partnerships — mainly commercial and dev relations.
[00:34] Sara Venkatesh: Sara, Solutions Architect. I'll be the technical lead on AetherScale side for this pilot.
[00:39] Maya Chen: Great, thanks. Goal today is to understand your partner motion, technical constraints, and see where Redwood fits — hosted, dedicated, or a private on-prem offering, plus what an initial pilot looks like.
[00:50] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Quick context — we're talking to a few inference platforms, want to offer turnkey onramp to our reseller customers. Primary asks: how easy is it to integrate, what telemetry and billing hooks you expose, and how we can bundle Redwood's runtime as an option in our console.
[01:10] Diego Alvarez: Understood. A couple of quick clarifying q's: do you expect us to embed the runtime in your console (white-label) or provide an API that your onramp calls?
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: Ideally API-first. We don't want to copy code, more like embed a 'deploy with Redwood' button. But for enterprise customers we may want an option for private deployments inside their VPC.
[01:30] Maya Chen: Ok API-first + private deploy option — that's a common pattern. We can support a hosted, dedicated, or private (VPC/on-prem) route. There are tradeoffs: hosted is fastest to ship, dedicated gives predictable throughput, private/VPC gives the most control and is typical for regulated customers.
[01:48] Sara Venkatesh: On the private side, our infra has custom NIC offloads and 200Gbps RDMA — we need to confirm compatibility. Also question on KMS/HSM integration for customer keys.
[01:58] Diego Alvarez: Good callouts. For NICs, we usually validate at the kernel and driver level; we have some partners with RDMA stacks but sometimes we need a small shim or config tweak. For KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via standard APIs — we can wire into your KMS/HSM, though on-prem HSM integrations may need some engineering work.
[02:21] Priya Nair: What's the expected effort? If it's multiple months to certify each NIC driver, that's a blocker for go-to-market.
[02:29] Diego Alvarez: It depends. If your NIC follows standard drivers and the card exposes the expected semantics, many times it's a config and validation — 2-4 weeks for a basic compatibility validation. If it's a custom firmware or vendor API, could be longer. We can use a lab validation early in the pilot to avoid surprises.
[02:46] Liam O'Connor: We can share a compatibility matrix and sample images. We'll also need pricing and margin for resellers — do you have standard partner discounts?
[02:56] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a partner commercial framework. High-level: referral commission + reseller margin for Dedicated/Private. Maya: I'll send the partner terms doc after this call.
[03:06] Priya Nair: Great. On the technical side, we want to understand latency and cost tradeoffs. Many of our customers care about token latency under 150ms for small chats, others care about throughput for batch embeddings.
[03:18] Diego Alvarez: Important to capture workload profiles. Our runtime offers KV cache, continuous batching, and quantization profiles. For sub-150ms SLOs you likely pick a lower-batch/low-latency configuration, maybe smaller model or 8-bit quant, and dedicated instances. For heavy throughput embeddings, batching aggressively + GPU pooling reduces cost.
[03:36] Sara Venkatesh: You mentioned KV cache — how intrusive is that for stateful requests? Some customers prefer stateless short-lived containers.
[03:44] Diego Alvarez: KV cache is optional but important for chat workloads with context. It requires the runtime to manage KV shards; for private deployments we can enable a local cache with sizing knobs. Stateless flows are supported too, we just lose cache speedups.
[03:56] Priya Nair: We also need to surface metrics in our console — token cost, latency percentiles, error rates, per-customer tenancy. How granular is Redwood telemetry?
[04:06] Maya Chen: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency p50/p95/p99, per-model dashboards, and trace IDs. We can provide a telemetry API or Flux exporter, and can push events into your datalake.
[04:17] Liam O'Connor: Any PIIs or logs stored with hosted inference? Our customers in finance need strict retention policies.
[04:24] Maya Chen: By default hosted keeps logs for X days, but for enterprise we offer configurable retention and audit logs. Private deployments keep logs under your control. We also support encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys.
[04:36] Diego Alvarez: One note — sometimes transcription of model names gets funky in our docs, so we'll include model mapping.
[04:42] Priya Nair: (laughs) helpful.
[04:46] Maya Chen: Let's talk pilot scope. Typical pilot for partners is: 1) compatibility validation with 1-2 hardware SKUs, 2) benchmark run on your lab machines with our benchmark scripts, 3) demo integration in your console (button + API), 4) limited customer pilot. Thoughts?
[05:00] Sara Venkatesh: That seems reasonable. On benchmarks — can you share the scripts? We prefer reproducible workloads.
[05:06] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll share a benchmark template and a set of tests — latency microbenchmarks, throughput harness, and mixed workloads. We'll include seq len distributions to mimic chat vs batch embeddings.
[05:16] Liam O'Connor: When you mention mixed workloads, do you have a suggestion for batching parameters for an inference pool? Some of our customers will want autoscale but predictable latency.
[05:26] Diego Alvarez: We recommend autoscale with floor capacity; set max batch latency to something like 20ms, and tune target batch size for the model. Our Optimize tool can suggest initial settings after a data profile.
[05:36] Priya Nair: Does Redwood have a partner SDK or marketplace listing we can include in our console?
[05:42] Maya Chen: We have a partner integration kit — API docs, SDK snippets, and a white-label console widget. We can provide a packaged OVA for on-prem demos too.
[05:52] Sara Venkatesh: OVA would be useful for offline tests. On the KMS/HSM point — customers may require FIPS certs, is that supported?
[06:00] Diego Alvarez: We can support FIPS-compatible crypto stacks in Private deployments; hosted may have options depending on region and compliance package. We'll share the SOC2/ISO docs too.
[06:09] Priya Nair: Great. A few red flags we've seen with other vendors: hidden per-token surcharges, no clear rollbacks for model regressions, and poor RBAC for multi-tenanted resellers. Can you address those concerns?
[06:23] Maya Chen: Totally valid. Our pricing is transparent — per-token plus optional ERAs for specialized models. We provide rollout tools (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) and RBAC support with SSO/SAML and scoped API keys for reseller scenarios.
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: For a reseller model, we need per-customer billing exports and reseller invoicing.
[06:42] Maya Chen: We support billing exports in CSV and billing APIs; we can do reseller invoicing as part of the partner program.
[06:48] Sara Venkatesh: On the network side, does Redwood require specific ports or egress rules for the runtime to talk to control plane? For air-gapped customers we may need full offline ops.
[06:58] Diego Alvarez: For Private on-prem with full offline, there's an air-gap package. For VPC deployments, we require outbound to our control plane on a limited set of endpoints or a private link option. We'll document required ports.
[07:12] Priya Nair: What about model hosting — can partners bring their own model artifacts? Some customers use custom finetuned models or proprietary weights.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Partners/customers can bring their own model artifacts. We support pinned model versions and can host models in private registries or your object storage. We'll need to sign an MOU for IP handling when models are proprietary.
[07:33] Liam O'Connor: Ok, good. Another question — do you have a minimum committed capacity for Dedicated pools? Some of our mid-market customers balk at large monthly minimums.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Dedicated has tiered commits; we can do lower baseline commits for channel partners with different pricing. We can align on burst/overage policies.
[07:52] Diego Alvarez: From an SE perspective, I'd like to get SSH access to a lab image or sample card to run the initial compatibility checks.
[07:59] Sara Venkatesh: We can spin up a lab node and provide creds.
[08:03] Diego Alvarez: Perfect. For benchmarks, we'll need 3 sample models (small chat model, medium-latency generalist, and embedding model) and sequences. We'll supply the runner and expected CSV outputs.
[08:14] Maya Chen: We'll share the benchmark template and the playbook link after call.
[08:19] Priya Nair: On timelines — if we start next week, what's realistic to have a public joint pilot?
[08:25] Maya Chen: If compatibility validation goes smoothly, we could have an internal pilot in 3-4 weeks and a small public pilot 6-8 weeks out. Depends on resource allocation.
[08:35] Liam O'Connor: That timeline fits our Q3 push. Regarding commercial terms, are there co-marketing funds or joint webinars?
[08:43] Maya Chen: We have co-marketing programs for strategic partners, including joint webinars, case studies, and lead sharing depending on commitment.
[08:50] Priya Nair: Nice. A few nitty-gritty items: 1) we'll need a sample SLA for throughput/latency, 2) SOC2 and pen-test reports, 3) a single-page partner commercial term sheet.
[08:59] Maya Chen: We'll attach those to the follow-up email.
[09:03] Sara Venkatesh: One more technical — GPU driver versions. We currently run a mix of 470/510 driver stacks across SKUs. Any hard requirements?
[09:12] Diego Alvarez: We usually support a range of drivers but prefer LTS drivers; we'll test both versions. We'll note any kernel module incompatibilities.
[09:20] Priya Nair: Ok. For the console embedding, is there a React widget or a set of REST endpoints?
[09:27] Maya Chen: Both — we have a lightweight JS widget and full REST APIs. The widget can be themed and vendored into your console.
[09:33] Liam O'Connor: Great. On measurement — what success metrics do you track for partner pilots?
[09:39] Maya Chen: Adoption rate, latency SLO attainment, cost per inference, number of active customers onboarded, and a qualitative feedback score from pilot customers.
[09:47] Diego Alvarez: We'll also monitor error rates, queue lengths, and GPU utilization to tune pooling.
[09:52] Priya Nair: That works. Anything else from AetherScale?
[09:56] Sara Venkatesh: We want to make sure the partner integration doesn’t require deep changes to our billing engine. Can the billing hooks be event-based?
[10:04] Maya Chen: Yes, billing events and periodic exports both supported.
[10:08] Liam O'Connor: Ok, let's capture next concrete steps.
[10:11] Maya Chen: Recap — Redwood to share Partner Integration Playbook, benchmark template, SOC2/ISO docs, and partner term sheet. AetherScale to share hardware compatibility matrix, NIC details, and grant lab access. SEs to coordinate pilot plan and schedule validation.
[10:28] Priya Nair: Agreed. We'll aim to have the compatibility matrix by next Tuesday.
[10:33] Diego Alvarez: I'll draft the pilot test plan and send by Friday.
[10:36] Maya Chen: I'll circulate the partner commercial framework tomorrow.
[10:39] Liam O'Connor: Good. Any blockers or final concerns?
[10:42] Sara Venkatesh: Just checksum on timeline — we'll confirm resource allocation internally and revert.
[10:46] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the lab window.
[10:51] Priya Nair: Thanks, bye.
[10:53] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
